layers.note: A bunchgrass of the south Puget Sound prairies and oak savannas.

moisture.note: Dry, well-drained prairie soils on glacial outwash.

heat_load.note: Warm, sunny ground; favours slopes facing south and west.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

coldest_c.note: Widespread through the temperate and boreal zones: coldest-month means from about −20 °C (gone by −30 °C) to about 16 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 12 to 26 °C; gone below 8 °C, where summers are too short, and above 30 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,000 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 600.

degree_days_5.note: About 400 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 150.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.22, gone by 0.15.

summer_rain.note: No limit: it grows under summer-dry and summer-wet climates alike.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Prairie junegrass grows in grassland across temperate North America and Eurasia (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
